KP08 Speeding Up Backpropagation

Level: undergraduate, year 3

Pattern Recognition | Chapter 4, §4.7

Slides: read and download

Learning objectives

  • Explain why a narrow valley makes gradient descent slow and swinging.
  • Write the momentum update, work a few steps by hand, and explain why it speeds up the flat direction and cancels the steep one.
  • State the rules of the adaptive learning rate and of quickprop and know the price and limits of each.

KP08 Speeding Up Backpropagation

One-sentence summary: Gradient descent is slow and swings in a narrow valley; momentum adds α\alphaα times the previous step to this step, so the flat direction is enlarged and the steep one is cancelled; an adaptive learning rate lets μ\muμ adjust itself and quickprop estimates the valley floor from two slopes. Every speed-up costs extra complexity.

1. The narrow valley

Plain explanation: KP07 training took thousands of epochs, partly because gradient descent itself is slow.

  • Curvature: how sharply the cost surface bends. Where the curvature is large, a small step changes the cost a lot.
  • Narrow valley (ill-conditioned surface): very large curvature in one direction and very small in another, so the contours are flat ellipses; the source calls it ill-conditioned, meaning the eigenvalues of the Hessian differ a lot.

Example: for this lecture we designed J=12(w12+20w22)J=\tfrac12(w_1^2+20w_2^2)J=21​(w12​+20w22​) to show the mechanism: curvature 20 along w2w_2w2​ and 1 along w1w_1w1​, start (−4,1)(-4,1)(−4,1), μ=0.08\mu=0.08μ=0.08. Plain gradient descent needs 100 steps to reach ∣w∣<0.001|w|<0.001∣w∣<0.001 and swings along w2w_2w2​ (program).

Figure lec05-kp08-valley: contours and the path of plain gradient descent.

2. Why it swings

Steep direction: the gradient of w2w_2w2​ is 20w220w_220w2​, so w2←w2−0.08⋅20 w2=−0.6 w2w_2\leftarrow w_2-0.08\cdot20\,w_2=-0.6\,w_2w2​←w2​−0.08⋅20w2​=−0.6w2​: it flips sign every step and shrinks only to 0.6 times. Flat direction: w1←w1−0.08⋅1⋅w1=0.92 w1w_1\leftarrow w_1-0.08\cdot1\cdot w_1=0.92\,w_1w1​←w1​−0.08⋅1⋅w1​=0.92w1​, the same direction and only 8% smaller per step.

The dilemma: μ\muμ must stay below 2/20=0.12/20=0.12/20=0.1 or w2w_2w2​ swings ever wider; with μ=0.12\mu=0.12μ=0.12 the norm ∣w∣|w|∣w∣ exceeds 10810^8108 after 60 steps. But such a small step makes w1w_1w1​ slow.

Figure lec05-kp08-zigzag: w1w_1w1​ and w2w_2w2​ over the first 15 steps.

3. The momentum term

Momentum: gives the update inertia: besides the new gradient step, this step adds α\alphaα times the previous step.

Formal definition:

Δw(t)=α Δw(t−1)−μ g(t), \Delta w(t)=\alpha\,\Delta w(t-1)-\mu\,g(t), Δw(t)=αΔw(t−1)−μg(t),

ggg is the gradient and α\alphaα the momentum factor, 0.1 to 0.8 in practice; α=0\alpha=0α=0 is plain gradient descent.

By hand (μ=0.08\mu=0.08μ=0.08, α=0.6\alpha=0.6α=0.6): step 1 is (0.32,−1.6)(0.32,-1.6)(0.32,−1.6) and w=(−3.68,−0.6)w=(-3.68,-0.6)w=(−3.68,−0.6); step 2 is 0.6×(0.32,−1.6)−0.08×(−3.68,−12)=(0.4864,0)0.6\times(0.32,-1.6)-0.08\times(-3.68,-12)=(0.4864,0)0.6×(0.32,−1.6)−0.08×(−3.68,−12)=(0.4864,0), so the two pulls on w2w_2w2​ (inertia −0.96-0.96−0.96, gradient +0.96+0.96+0.96) cancel exactly. Step 3 is (0.5473,0.96)(0.5473,0.96)(0.5473,0.96) and w=(−2.646,0.36)w=(-2.646,0.36)w=(−2.646,0.36).

Figure lec05-kp08-mom-steps: table of the first three momentum steps.

4. Why it works: an exponentially weighted average of past gradients

Exponentially weighted average: the newest gradient weighs most and every older one is multiplied by α\alphaα once more, weights 1,α,α2,…1,\alpha,\alpha^2,\dots1,α,α2,….

Unrolled over TTT steps: Δw(T)=−μ∑tαtg(T−t)+αTΔw(0)\Delta w(T)=-\mu\sum_{t}\alpha^{t}g(T-t)+\alpha^{T}\Delta w(0)Δw(T)=−μ∑t​αtg(T−t)+αTΔw(0) and the last term is near 0 after a few steps. With an unchanging gradient (the flat direction) the total weight is 1+α+α2+⋯=1/(1−α)1+\alpha+\alpha^2+\cdots=1/(1-\alpha)1+α+α2+⋯=1/(1−α), which enlarges the learning rate by 1/(1−α)1/(1-\alpha)1/(1−α): 2.5 times for α=0.6\alpha=0.6α=0.6 and 5 times for α=0.8\alpha=0.8α=0.8 (checked with a fixed gradient over 80 steps). When the gradient alternates in sign (the steep direction) the weighted average cancels it. One mechanism, fast where it can be and steady where it must be.

Figure lec05-kp08-expo: weights 0.6t0.6^t0.6t and 0.8t0.8^t0.8t and the total weight under a fixed gradient.

5. Two paths

Same start and same μ=0.08\mu=0.08μ=0.08: plain needs 100 steps and momentum with α=0.6\alpha=0.6α=0.6 needs 28 (program). The red path swings along w2w_2w2​ many times while the green one shrinks the swing faster and also moves faster along w1w_1w1​. The price is one more stored array for the previous update and one more knob α\alphaα.

Figure lec05-kp08-two-paths: comparison of the two paths.

6. The best α\alphaα

Common misconception: a larger α\alphaα is always better. With μ=0.08\mu=0.08μ=0.08, α=0,0.3,0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9,0.95\alpha=0,0.3,0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9,0.95α=0,0.3,0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9,0.95 need 100, 65, 36, 28, 44, 63, 137 and 247 steps. α≥0.9\alpha\ge0.9α≥0.9 is slower than no momentum: too much inertia overshoots the valley floor and rocks like a pendulum before it stops. In practice 0.1 to 0.8 is common, the best value depends on the problem and must be tried, and the source reports speed-ups of 2 times or more.

Figure lec05-kp08-alpha-curve: steps needed for each α\alphaα.

7. Adaptive learning rate

Adaptive learning rate: adjust μ\muμ automatically from the ratio of the cost before and after a step:

μ(t)={1.05 μ(t−1),J(t)/J(t−1)<10.7 μ(t−1),J(t)/J(t−1)>1.04μ(t−1),otherwise \mu(t)=\begin{cases}1.05\,\mu(t-1), & J(t)/J(t-1)<1\\ 0.7\,\mu(t-1), & J(t)/J(t-1)>1.04\\ \mu(t-1), & \text{otherwise}\end{cases} μ(t)=⎩⎨⎧​1.05μ(t−1),0.7μ(t−1),μ(t−1),​J(t)/J(t−1)<1J(t)/J(t−1)>1.04otherwise​

Typical values ri=1.05r_i=1.05ri​=1.05, rd=0.7r_d=0.7rd​=0.7, c=1.04c=1.04c=1.04 (source). The rule is asymmetric: slow growth when better, hard braking when worse; when the cost rises this lecture rejects the step and zeroes the momentum (one of the source's suggestions).

Results (program): from μ0=0.02\mu_0=0.02μ0​=0.02 plain needs 411 steps and adaptive 61; from μ0=0.12\mu_0=0.12μ0​=0.12 plain blows up while adaptive rejects 12 steps and converges in 95; from μ0=0.08\mu_0=0.08μ0​=0.08, already near the best, adaptive needs 93 steps, hardly better than plain 100.

Figure lec05-kp08-adaptive: semi-log curve of ∣w∣|w|∣w∣ against steps.

8. quickprop and a comparison of five methods

quickprop: treat every weight as independent; the last two slopes estimate the bottom of a parabola and the weight jumps there:

Δw(t)=α(t) Δw(t−1),α(t)=min⁡{g(t)g(t−1)−g(t), αmax⁡}, αmax⁡≈1.75. \Delta w(t)=\alpha(t)\,\Delta w(t-1),\qquad \alpha(t)=\min\Bigl\{\frac{g(t)}{g(t-1)-g(t)},\ \alpha_{\max}\Bigr\},\ \alpha_{\max}\approx1.75. Δw(t)=α(t)Δw(t−1),α(t)=min{g(t−1)−g(t)g(t)​, αmax​}, αmax​≈1.75.

Example (w2w_2w2​): step 1 is an ordinary step 1→−0.61\to-0.61→−0.6 with slope 20→−1220\to-1220→−12; α=−12/(20+12)=−0.375\alpha=-12/(20+12)=-0.375α=−12/(20+12)=−0.375 and Δ=−0.375×(−1.6)=+0.6\Delta=-0.375\times(-1.6)=+0.6Δ=−0.375×(−1.6)=+0.6, so step 2 lands exactly on 0. The whole quadratic example takes 5 steps (plain μ=0.02\mu=0.02μ=0.02 411, adaptive 61, plain μ=0.08\mu=0.08μ=0.08 100, momentum 28). But every slice of this example is exactly a parabola, ideal for quickprop; real costs are not quadratic. Every speed-up costs extra complexity.

Figure lec05-kp08-compare: steps of the five methods.

Extension: Newton's method, practice and worked solution

Newton's method: use the curvature (the Hessian matrix HHH) to compute the valley floor directly, Δw=−H−1g\Delta w=-H^{-1}gΔw=−H−1g, and a quadratic is solved in one step. Here H=diag(1,20)H=\mathrm{diag}(1,20)H=diag(1,20) and Δw=−w\Delta w=-wΔw=−w, one step to the origin; the price is computing, storing and inverting the Hessian. quickprop can be seen as a one-dimensional Newton method per weight. The source also lists conjugate gradient, the Newton family, Kalman filtering and Levenberg–Marquardt, mostly needing Hessian elements; delta-delta and delta-bar-delta give every weight its own learning rate, grown when its gradient keeps its sign and shrunk when it flips.

Figure lec05-kp08-secant: the parabola along w2w_2w2​ and the quickprop jump.
